solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Display attitude that's no longer relevant?

parts.note: something former or past is an ex, no longer current
an attitude or stance is a position

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a view they once held is now simply out of date.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one question about an outdated view; the answer is built in reverse clue order, the 'no longer relevant' part coming first.
explanation.definitionFit: An exposition is a public exhibition or show, a synonym for a display.

clue.text: Judge, Conservative replacing Liberal, to leave premises

indicators.note: replacing means the Conservative letter takes the place of the Liberal one

parts.note: to evaluate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: A judge, Tory taking a Liberal's seat, is told to leave the building.
explanation.walkthrough: The political swap looks like an election; it just swaps the L in EVALUATE for C.
explanation.definitionFit: To evacuate is to clear out of a building or area, departing the premises.

clue.text: Undermine plan to return Argentine parts

indicators.note: to return here means the two words are read backwards, as this is a down clue going back up

parts.note: to sap is to undermine or weaken
a map is a plan or chart

explanation.surface: A scheme to sabotage the return of parts of Argentina, perhaps the Falklands.
explanation.walkthrough: SAP and MAP are written backwards together.
explanation.definitionFit: The pampas are the vast grassy plains of Argentina, regions of that country.

clue.text: Heroic storyteller, in black, placed in grave

indicators.note: placed in means the in-and-black pieces go inside the word for grave

parts.note: grave means serious or sad
taken as written
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A storyteller, dressed in black, is laid to rest in a grave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' looks like a burial place; it is the adjective, sad.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinbad the Sailor of the Arabian Nights narrates his own seven heroic voyages.

clue.text: Ruined page in ripped back of tattered dictionary

indicators.note: in means the page letter goes inside the word for ripped

parts.note: tore means ripped

indicators.note: back of points to the final letter of tattered

parts.note: the OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

explanation.surface: A page is torn out at the back of a battered dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: TOR(P)E, then D, the back of 'tattered', then OED.
explanation.definitionFit: Torpedoed figuratively means wrecked or sunk, as plans are destroyed.

clue.text: Ill omen with crew's latest arrival

indicators.note: ill means badly, so the letters are put into bad order

explanation.surface: A sailor's superstition: the newest arrival among the crew is a bad omen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ill omen' reads as one phrase, but 'Ill' is the anagram signal on OMEN plus CREW.
explanation.definitionFit: A newcomer is someone who has recently come, the most recent arrival.

clue.text: Agriculturalist, never right, comes to prominence

indicators.note: never having any right says every R (right) is removed from the word

parts.note: an agriculturalist works the land, a farmer

explanation.surface: A farmer becomes well known in the wider world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'never right' removes both Rs from FARMER, not just one.
explanation.definitionFit: Fame is renown, being widely known, which is prominence in public life.

clue.text: School member admits dirty look and gesture

indicators.note: admits means the school member takes the dirty look inside

parts.note: a fish is a member of a school of fish
to lour is to scowl, a dirty look

explanation.surface: A pupil lets slip a scowl and a rude gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School member' suggests a pupil; it is a fish, since fish swim in schools.
explanation.definitionFit: A flourish is a showy, sweeping movement of the hand, a dramatic gesture.

clue.text: Dairy product from base in Irish province

indicators.note: in means the base letter sits inside the province's name

parts.note: Munster is one of the four provinces of Ireland
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A cheese comes from a dairy base in southern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: E as 'base' is the mathematical constant e, base of natural logs.
explanation.definitionFit: Muenster is a soft cheese from Alsace, one product of a dairy.

clue.text: Closely allied, two divisions circling home

indicators.note: circling means the pair of divisions goes round the word for home
two asks for the word for divisions to be given twice

parts.note: an arm is a division or branch of an organisation
in, as in staying in, means at home

explanation.surface: Two military divisions surround a base and are thus closely allied.
explanation.walkthrough: IN sits between the two ARMs.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking with linked arms pictures two people close together, so the idiom means closely associated.

clue.text: Unnatural Germanic god peripheral to Ring?

indicators.note: being peripheral to something means lying round its edge, so the god's name surrounds the ring

parts.note: Woden is the Anglo-Saxon form of the chief Germanic god Odin
a ring is round, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A Wagnerian complaint: the Germanic god in the Ring cycle seems stilted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' tempts toward Wagner's operas, where Wotan appears; here it is just the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden performance is stiff and stilted, lacking natural ease, so unnatural.

clue.text: Stubbs for one was about to enter without warning

parts.note: Una Stubbs was a British actress, known from Till Death Us Do Part and Sherlock

indicators.note: to enter means the short word for about goes inside the word was

parts.note: taken as written
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: The painter Stubbs was about to burst in on someone unexpectedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stubbs' suggests George Stubbs, the horse painter; it is the actress Una Stubbs, a well-known British TV face.
explanation.definitionFit: Caught unawares means taken by surprise, with no prior notice, i.e. without warning.

clue.text: Where dragonfly might land, making surge forward?

definitions.meaning: on a rush, the waterside reed where a dragonfly perches
a forceful forward rush or charge

explanation.surface: A dragonfly's landing spot is pictured, perhaps sparking a sudden charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the word into two: ON RUSH, a reed a dragonfly could settle upon.
explanation.definitionFit: An onrush is a sudden strong forward movement, as of water or a crowd, a surge.

clue.text: Clubs held by United — but not now?

indicators.note: being held by means the clubs letter sits inside the word for united

parts.note: united means made one, at one
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A football fan muses that United once held the clubs, but no longer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' looks like a football club; it gives ONE, as in 'at one'.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means formerly, at some past time, which is a time other than the present.

clue.text: Singer, bad lot, supporting old Nicaraguan guerrilla

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means the jumbled lot sits beneath the guerrilla

parts.note: the Contras were rebels fighting Nicaragua's Sandinista government in the 1980s

indicators.note: bad means the letters of lot go wrong, rearranged

explanation.surface: A singer from a bad crowd backs an old Nicaraguan rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' scrambles LOT to LTO, placed under CONTRA.
explanation.definitionFit: A contralto is the lowest female voice, and by extension a singer with it.

clue.text: Bean and cheese served with meat that's no good

parts.note: Edam is a Dutch cheese

indicators.note: meat that's no good means the meat has its G removed

parts.note: game is meat from hunted animals

explanation.surface: A plate of beans and cheese is served beside some meat that has gone off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meat' gives GAME, and 'no good' strips its G to leave AME.
explanation.definitionFit: Edamame are young green soya beans served in the pod, a Japanese dish.

clue.text: New player included in side, but antagonised

indicators.note: included in means the letters are found inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A newcomer is picked for the team but upsets teammates.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'siDE BUT ANTagonised'.
explanation.definitionFit: A debutant is someone making a first appearance, such as a player's debut match.

clue.text: Drunk to devour onion where starter denied in fruit

indicators.note: to devour means the word for drunk swallows the trimmed onion

parts.note: merry means tipsy, slightly drunk

indicators.note: the starter denied means the first letter is removed

parts.note: an onion is a bulb

explanation.surface: A drunk wolfs down onion, minus its first bit, among some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'onion' gives the general word for its kind of root, not a variety; 'where starter denied' strips that word's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A mulberry is a dark berry-like fruit of the mulberry tree.

clue.text: Musical heroine with cold welcome for Mexican player

parts.note: Maria is the heroine of the musicals The Sound of Music and West Side Story
hi is a greeting or welcome

explanation.surface: A musical's heroine gives a chilly welcome to a Mexican performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cold welcome' splits into C and HI.
explanation.definitionFit: Mariachi are Mexican street bands, and one member is a mariachi player.

clue.text: Golden vegetable seen in cultivated land

parts.note: or is the heraldic term for gold
chard is a leafy green vegetable

explanation.surface: A golden vegetable is spotted growing in a farmed plot.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is heraldry's word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard is a plot planted with fruit trees, a piece of cultivated ground.

clue.text: Rats devouring dead swimmer

indicators.note: devouring means the exclamation takes the word for dead inside

parts.note: rats and drat are both exclamations of annoyance
gone means dead

explanation.surface: Rats eat a dead creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rats' looks like the animals; it is the oath, DRAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragonet is a small, often colourful sea fish, so a swimmer.

clue.text: Wystan Hugh leaves university for foreign climes

indicators.note: leaves means the university letter departs from the poet's surname

parts.note: Wystan Hugh were the forenames of the poet W. H. Auden

explanation.surface: The poet Auden quits his university post to go abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Auden did leave Oxford and Britain for America, which feeds the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Aden, a port city in Yemen, stands for a hot distant place, an example of foreign parts.

clue.text: Nice neighbour one scratched among dogs

indicators.note: scratched among means the letter for one is struck out from the dogs

parts.note: canines are dogs
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A neighbour, being kind, removes one dog from a pack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like the adjective; it is the French city on the Riviera.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannes is a Riviera resort close to Nice, so its neighbour.

clue.text: Scoundrel in American intelligence finds bug

indicators.note: in means the scoundrel sits inside the agency's initials

parts.note: the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency
a cad is a scoundrel

explanation.surface: A rogue inside the CIA discovers a listening device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bug' in a spy surface suggests a hidden microphone; it is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A cicada is a loud chirping insect, and bug loosely means any insect.

clue.text: Letter to Greek business graduate, one in City

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
an MBA is a Master of Business Administration
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A letter goes to a Greek MBA holder working in the City of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City' looks like London's financial district; it is the definition, the Indian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Mumbai, formerly Bombay, is India's largest metropolis and financial centre.

clue.text: Apprehensive about daughter going to Berkshire town

parts.note: Reading is a large town in the English county of Berkshire

explanation.surface: A parent is nervous about their daughter heading off to Reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' belongs to the definition: dreading something means fearing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreading something is anticipating it with fear, being apprehensive about it.

clue.text: Unfinished food placed alongside great stuff

parts.note: fab, short for fabulous, means great

indicators.note: unfinished means the word for food loses its last letter

parts.note: rice is a staple food

explanation.surface: A half-eaten meal sits next to something wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: RICE loses its final E to give RIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuff in the old sense is cloth or material, which is what fabric is.

clue.text: Distress over large insect found in banana

indicators.note: over here means the word for distress goes all over, round the large insect

parts.note: pain is distress or suffering
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: Alarm at discovering a big bug in a banana.
explanation.walkthrough: 'large insect' looks like one idea but splits into L and ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A plantain is a starchy cooking variety of banana.

clue.text: What guest might do, perhaps consuming tons

indicators.note: consuming means the word for perhaps takes in the letter for tons

parts.note: say means for example or perhaps, as in 'say, ten people'

explanation.surface: A guest who might eat tons of food is pictured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' gives SAY, as in 'take, say, five'.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest stops for a while at a host's home or hotel, which is to remain there.

clue.text: Often changing precise time to restrain prisoner

indicators.note: to restrain means the word for precise time holds the prisoner inside

parts.note: an instant is a precise moment
a con, short for convict, is a prisoner

explanation.surface: The exact moment arrives to lock up a prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to restrain' pictures the moment holding the convict, which is just what the letters do.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inconstant is fickle, varying from moment to moment.
